text: nice that is working great the one thing though uh im only seeing top for floors which would mean the bottom is gone? and then that means how would i use floor pieces when i am placing lets say a floor as the roof when there are multiple stories in a building for example :? they use to have like 3 faces if i remember correctly
resolution: Restored the hmsc three-face model on plates: floors and roofs expose top/bottom/edges again, so a floor placed as a ceiling in a multi-story build paints its underside, and the edge band is its own face. The render side needed zero new geometry — pieceShapes has always decomposed a plate into a top sliver, bottom sliver, and core slab; the gap was authoring-side: pieceSlots only advertised the top role, and pieceSkins' resolution chains let any face bleed onto any other. Roles now mirror what each kind's decomposition can actually wear: floor/roof top+bottom+edges, the wall family (wall/arch/fence/railing) gains sides for the core and end caps, corner drops its dead back role for the single surface its one body box has. pieceSkins chains are role-explicit (bottom sliver reads bottom, core reads edges/sides, no cross-face tails), so targeting top and picking brick lands ONLY on top — the exact semantics the user ruled for the quick menu — while an untargeted pick still covers every face via the all-roles assign. Quick menu chips and Inspector slot rows widen automatically off pieceSlotRoles (three 68px chips fit the 240px menu exactly). Editor cart bundles clean; framework compile verified alongside req_2746 (rjit ship editor raw binary, exit 0).
